description: Operational data sources used in the ShipCrawler IEEE Access validation (Access-2026-38078, 63-vessel cohort, June-July 2026). This is the source set that produced the findings reported in the paper — distinct from the general OSINT catalog in sources.json.

paper.title: ShipCrawler: Agentic Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) Platform for Maritime Cybersecurity — Implementation and Empirical Validation
paper.framework: OSINT Maritime Framework (Nasr et al., IEEE Access 2026, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3673557)

sources.name: Equasis
sources.role: Primary vessel identity: IMO, flag, call sign, MMSI, GT, DWT, type, year built, management companies, classification societies, PSC inspection history
sources.rateLimit: 30-60 s between automated lookups; account lock after ~10 login attempts in a short window

sources.name: Shodan
sources.role: Host intelligence, port enumeration, CVE detection; queries by vessel name, MMSI, IMO, call sign, historical names; maritime filters (Cobham SAILOR 900, Signal K port 3000, country:EE)

categories.name: AIS tracking

sources.name: MarineTraffic
sources.access: Web details page by MMSI (CloakBrowser anti-bot bypass required)
sources.role: Position, speed, course, destination, port call history

sources.name: VesselFinder
sources.role: Position, speed, course, destination, port call history

sources.name: MyShipTracking
sources.role: Position, speed, course, destination, port call history

categories.verificationRule: 3+ independent AIS sources agreeing = HIGH confidence on identity/position

sources.name: Firecrawl
sources.role: Maritime news, company websites, port authority pages

sources.name: OCCRP (Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project)
sources.role: Shell-company network identification (e.g., 31 Azerbaijan-registered entities managing sanctioned tankers)

sources.name: MISP
sources.role: Threat intelligence sharing: IMO, MMSI, AIS dark periods, sanctions regimes

sources.name: Elasticsearch / Zeek / Wazuh
sources.role: Generated indicators-and-detection rules formatted for direct import

notes: All sources are publicly accessible; no data-sharing agreement required.
A negative Shodan result is reported as 'no vessel-attributable exposure identified' — not as proof of absence.
The 63-vessel cohort was deliberately limited to already-sanctioned vessels to avoid unapproved scanning of non-sanctioned operators.
